summary: This document specifies how to use the AES-GMAC message authentication code with the Cryptographic Message Syntax (CMS) described in RFC 5652. It defines the conventions needed so a CMS message can carry an authentication tag produced by AES-GMAC, letting a receiver check that the content was not changed.

eli5.summary: A message can carry a secret stamp that proves nobody scribbled on it along the way. This document explains how to put one particular kind of stamp, called AES-GMAC, onto messages in a common secure-message format.

questions: how to use gmac in cryptographic message syntax
